messages:
Anna: Quick design q — Console wants a tiny badge + expandable hint for client-visible errors. Can the API provide a stable, compact surface?

Mike: Today we mostly rely on HTTP codes (429/503/409) and some internal 5xx flavors. SDK normalizes many to `TransientError` which leaves Console guessing on badge semantics.

Tao: Reminder: we added 429 subcodes last quarter (burst vs budget). SDK ignores subcodes right now; we should avoid making clients parse too many numeric signals.

Jen: Proposal: small, explicit contract in the error body. Add `status_category` (enum: "throttle", "degrade", "quota", "internal_fallback") and `short_hint` (<=120 chars). Optional `badge_text` (<=24 chars) for the compact badge, plus `help_url`. Keep HTTP codes unchanged so infra can keep using them.

Mike: Implementation note: several services only emit HTTP codes. We'll add a gateway middleware to synthesize `status_category` from routing metadata and headers. Gate it behind a feature flag `error_cat_v1` for a canary rollout.

Anna: UX constraints: absolutely no internal pool/node/job identifiers in client strings. Hints must be user-facing and actionable (ex: "Retry after 2s, reduce concurrency"). No PII, no tenant keys.

Tao: Telemetry plan: include `status_category` in trace spans. Sample the `short_hint` text for quality at 1% for free-tier accounts and 10% for paid; emit aggregated counts and region breakdowns. Internal-only fields (route variant etc.) must live under `x-internal.*` and never be sent to public clients.

Jen: Example payload for Console/SDK contract:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 429,
    "status_category": "throttle",
    "badge_text": "Rate-limited",
    "short_hint": "Burst limit hit. Retry in 2s or lower concurrency.",
    "retry_after": 2,
    "help_url": "https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/client-errors"
  }
}
```

Mike: SDK behaviour: if service doesn't include these fields, SDK should fall back to heuristics (status code + headers) and Console should render a generic badge labelled "Failure" with tooltip "Details unavailable — upgrade for richer hints". That keeps backwards compatibility.

Anna: Add a linter rule in CI to scan `short_hint` and `badge_text` for forbidden tokens (pool names, region ids, internal job ids). In canary it should be a warning; after stable rollout it becomes blocking on main.

Tao: Security/privacy: do not include request bodies, prompts, or user content in `short_hint`. Enforce max length and character whitelist; strip non-printables.

Mike: On headers: do not expose internal headers to clients. `x-internal-*` only to logs/metrics. No `X-Redwood-Route-Fallback` in public responses. If needed, put it in logs or internal-only headers behind `allow-internal`.

Jen: I'll update the SDK error mapping table and add unit tests asserting that SDK never displays internal substrings in badges/hints.

deploy-bot: deployment: error-cat-middleware v1 -> canary on prod-a :rocket:

Anna: Monitor sampling for 2hrs. If any sampled `short_hint` contains internal tokens we'll rollback immediately.

Jen: I'll draft the runbook page mapping each `status_category` to mitigations and example retry patterns; assigning review to Tao.

Tao: Will review the runbook. Also propose a small Console card: category distribution plus a redacted hint-sample widget so product can iterate on wording.

Mike: Rolling feature flag on Thursday. I'll put a short rollout plan in #release-war-room and a postmortem checklist for any privacy leakage.

Anna: Thanks everyone. Sync after the canary window. End thread.
